headline: 30+ garment factories shut down in Ashulia amid wage protests
summary: Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000 and an end to blacklisting, leading to clashes with police and road blockades.
details: At least 30 garment factories in and around Kathgara in Ashulia have declared a holiday today as workers protest for a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.
The unrest began in the morning, with workers from Naim Knitwear initially stopping work before expanding their protest to other factories in the area.
Clashes broke out between workers and police, with reports of bricks and stones being thrown. One police officer was hospitalized after being struck on the head.
Industrial police also recovered three crude-bomb-like objects from the road in front of a Nasa Group factory in Nishchintapur, which have been reported to the Anti-Terrorism Unit.
Beyond Ashulia, garment workers also blocked several roads in Dhaka’s Mirpur area to voice the same demands.
Workers are protesting the delay in forming a minimum wage board, which the labour minister had previously announced would be formed by October.
A meeting at the Ministry of Labour last night announced that the process of forming the board would begin by Sunday, but workers claim the message has not reached them.
caption:
30+ factories shut down and crude bombs found as garment workers demand Tk 30,000 minimum wage.

At least 30 garment factories in and around Kathgara in Ashulia have declared a holiday today as workers protest for a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.

The unrest began in the morning, with workers from Naim Knitwear initially stopping work before expanding their protest to other factories in the area.

Clashes broke out between workers and police, with reports of bricks and stones being thrown. One police officer was hospitalized after being struck on the head.

Industrial police also recovered three crude-bomb-like objects from the road in front of a Nasa Group factory in Nishchintapur, which have been reported to the Anti-Terrorism Unit.

Beyond Ashulia, garment workers also blocked several roads in Dhaka’s Mirpur area to voice the same demands.

Workers are protesting the delay in forming a minimum wage board, which the labour minister had previously announced would be formed by October.

A meeting at the Ministry of Labour last night announced that the process of forming the board would begin by Sunday, but workers claim the message has not reached them.

topic: HSC exam pass rate drops significantly
headline_marked: Over 5 lakh fail as [[HSC pass rate hits 22-year low]]
headline: Over 5 lakh fail as HSC pass rate hits 22-year low
summary: Pass rate for general education boards dropped to 51.62%, while GPA-5 achievers also hit an eight-year low.
details: The pass rate for this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examinations has fallen to a 22-year low, with over 5,07,281 students failing under the nine general education boards.
According to results published on Saturday, the pass rate stood at 51.62 percent, a significant drop from last year's 57.12 percent.
Data from the Bangladesh Bureau of Educational Information and Statistics (BANBEIS) shows the last time the pass rate was this low was in 2004, when it stood at 47.73 percent.
Across all 11 education boards, including Madrasa and Technical boards, 5,94,113 students failed, bringing the combined pass rate to 52.12 percent.
The number of students securing GPA-5 also hit an eight-year low, with only 40,084 students achieving the top grade across all 11 boards compared to 69,097 last year.
Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon described the results as unsatisfactory and stated that the government will take steps to address learning gaps.
caption:
Over 5 lakh students failed this year's HSC exams—the lowest pass rate in 22 years.

The pass rate for this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examinations has fallen to a 22-year low, with over 5,07,281 students failing under the nine general education boards.

According to results published on Saturday, the pass rate stood at 51.62 percent, a significant drop from last year's 57.12 percent.

Data from the Bangladesh Bureau of Educational Information and Statistics (BANBEIS) shows the last time the pass rate was this low was in 2004, when it stood at 47.73 percent.

Across all 11 education boards, including Madrasa and Technical boards, 5,94,113 students failed, bringing the combined pass rate to 52.12 percent.

The number of students securing GPA-5 also hit an eight-year low, with only 40,084 students achieving the top grade across all 11 boards compared to 69,097 last year.

Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon described the results as unsatisfactory and stated that the government will take steps to address learning gaps.
